newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasuries open steady with no data scheduled.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries open steady with no data scheduled.

text.p: U.S. Treasury prices opened steady on Monday amid light trading volume with no economic data scheduled for release.

The short end could see more support from fears of further erosion in stock prices. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 247 points on Friday, leading many investors to seek the security of the short end of the Treasury spectrum.

Otherwise, analysts said there was little to trade on this week. The Federal Reserve's policy-making Federal Open Market Committee meets on Tuesday, but no further tightening of monetary policy was expected.
Patrick Dimick, a trader at UBS Securities, said many dealers may think the rally sparked by the falloff in equities on Friday has fizzled.
He said the Standard & Poor's futures contract held on overnight in Tokyo.
"Some bought bonds on speculation on Friday," but that buying may be done, he said.
"It seems the yield curve is trying to flatten a touch. The front end of the market saw good overseas buying," said a trader at a primary dealership.
The trader said there was a favorable backdrop to the bond market overall, however.
"The curve should flatten. We'll have to see how the market reacts, but if the Teamsters come out with a big win in the UPS strike, the market won't like it at all," he said.
He said talk of a coupon pass at some point soon also was helping market sentiment.
The Treasury was scheduled on Monday to conduct its weekly auction of three- and six-month bills with a bidding deadline of 1300 EDT/1700 GMT. The size of this week's auction was to be $16 billion.
